name: Trans-Iranian Railway
description: This 1,394-kilometre railway links the Caspian Sea to the Persian Gulf, climbing across two mountain ranges and passing through forests, highlands and plains. Built between 1927 and 1938, it needed 174 large bridges and 224 tunnels, 11 of them spiral tunnels that loop inside the mountains. Iran paid for it with national taxes rather than foreign loans, though 43 contractors from many countries helped build it.
